extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, peer reviewers, authors, and scholarly publishers (medical/nursing/biomedical fields)
extracted.subtask_description: Narrative review summarising innovations, models, anonymity schemes, incentives, training, and core competencies for peer review in biomedical publishing; intended to inform changes to peer review processes and reviewer development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Openness (evaluation axis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Openness — whether review content, editorial decisions, and identities are made public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a comparative metric across peer review approaches and innovations (tables compare Openness alongside Anonymity, Accountability, Bias, Time, Incentive). Greater openness is associated with transparency, tempering strong criticism, potentially improved review quality, and increased participation; but may conflict with certain blinding schemes and raise concerns about exposing reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity (evaluation axis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anonymity — degree to which authors, reviewers, and editors are identifiable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparative metric: single-/double-/triple-blind and various open-blinding hybrids affect bias, accountability, and willingness to criticize. Choice of anonymity has trade-offs (e.g., double-blind can reduce gender/ethnicity bias but may lessen COI awareness).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability (evaluation axis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accountability — whether reviewers and editors are publicly accountable for their reports and decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Higher accountability (e.g., open reports) may encourage constructive reviews and reduce redundancy; lack of accountability can allow nonconstructive criticism and reduced quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias (evaluation axis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bias — susceptibility of review processes to personal, professional, gender/ethnicity, or other biases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluated across models; double-blind can reduce some biases, open review may temper strong criticism, but financial or social incentives can introduce new biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time (evaluation axis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Time — how quickly the review and publication process proceeds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to judge innovations (e.g., whether they shorten reviewing time, avoid redundant reviews). Delays arise from reviewer scarcity, multiple revisions, and redundant re-review of rejected papers; cascading/portable reviews aim to reduce time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incentive (evaluation axis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Incentive — whether reviewers receive recognition, credit, or financial compensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considered when comparing approaches: incentives can hasten reviews or improve participation but may affect review quality or introduce conflicts; forms include acknowledgement, ORCID/DOI crediting, certificates, or monetary payment/waivers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traditional peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Traditional peer review — in-house editorial assessment, external reviewers chosen by the editor, and final chief editor assessment; confidential process with unpublished reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Features: initial editorial appraisal to filter low-quality submissions; confidentiality; reviews/reports not published. Risks: potential low review quality, less accountability, redundant reviews, longer times depending on reviewer availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Open peer review — disclosure of editors' and reviewers' names to authors and often publication of reviewers' reports alongside articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thought to increase transparency, temper strong criticism, improve review quality, avoid redundant reviews, speed up publication, incentivize reviewers, and enable interactive discussion between authors and reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-peer review commenting
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-peer review commenting — informal commenting or discussion on a publicly available pre-publication manuscript draft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitates early feedback and broader participation; is informal and may not substitute for formal peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-publication peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-publication peer review — formal, editorially invited evaluation of research by selected experts before publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Traditional form of peer review; maintains editorial selection/filtering before publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-publication peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-publication peer review — formal and optionally invited expert evaluation after publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows continued scrutiny and correction after publication; may not shorten initial publication time but increases engagement and detection of issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-publication commenting
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-publication commenting — informal discussion of published research independent of formal peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Increases transparency and wider participation (e.g., via social media), but risks irrelevant or non-expert commentary and requires careful moderation or curation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative review
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaborative review — referees, editors, and external readers provide interactive comments leading to consensus decision and a single set of revisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promotes constructive, integrated feedback and consensus; may be more supportive but can expose studies prematurely or challenge experts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portable review
rubrics_metrics.description: Portable review — authors pay for a standard single-blind review (e.g., via services like Rubriq) that can be submitted to collaborating journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims to cut redundant reviews and speed resubmission between journals; risks shifting focus toward monetized reviewing and non-academic incentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation services review
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation services review — post-publication evaluation and recommendation of significant articles often through a peer-nominated consortium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides selective endorsement and discovery of important work post-publication; typically does not change anonymity but offers curation and recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decoupled post-publication review
rubrics_metrics.description: Decoupled post-publication review — adding notes directly to highlighted sections of the work which can be kept private or made public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables targeted annotation and commentary; may be used privately or publicly for granular review and discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cascading peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Cascading peer review — redirecting peer-reviewed but rejected papers to more suitable venues, sometimes passing on referee reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduces redundant reviews and time/cost by sharing reports across journals or within publisher families; can shorten publication pipeline for authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent peer review (commercial platforms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent peer review — companies provide pre-submission peer review for a fee (e.g., Rubriq, Peerage of Science) or provide reports to assist journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can dissociate review from journal, enable faster validation/detection of integrity issues, and provide scorecards; raises concerns about commercialization and equity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interactive peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Interactive peer review — reviewers interact online with authors and other scientists to produce open/collaborative review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports collaborative improvement of manuscripts but can prematurely expose work and provoke debate among experts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-blind peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Single-blind peer review — authors are known but reviewers are anonymous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can allow strong or biased comments by anonymous reviewers; common in traditional models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-blind peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Double-blind peer review — both reviewers and authors are anonymous to each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can achieve greater equality across gender/ethnicity and reduce some biases, but may reduce awareness of conflicts of interest and can be difficult to fully anonymize.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triple-blind peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Triple-blind peer review — authors and their affiliations are kept hidden from the editor as well as from reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maximizes anonymity but runs counter to open peer review and may impede editorial oversight of conflicts or author expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private open peer review (consent-based reveal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Private open peer review — names of authors and reviewers are revealed upon their consent, allowing interaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows free interaction if both consent; balances transparency with voluntariness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unattributed peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Unattributed peer review — reviewers' reports are made public anonymously upon consent after publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enhances transparency of review content while preserving reviewer anonymity; downside is failure to give reviewer credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional peer review (opt-in openness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional peer review — reviewers can choose to make their review and name public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May avoid bias and promote incentivization of reviewers while preserving choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-publication open peer review (blinding variant)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-publication open peer review (blinding variant) — referees are disclosed to authors before publication and review history is made public after publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives credit to reviewers and opens pre-publication discussion; increases transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-publication open peer review (blinding variant)
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-publication open peer review — referees' names and reports are made public after publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows addition of critiques from other researchers and post-publication discussion; increases accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review by endorsement
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review by endorsement — reviews are pre-arranged and the article is approved by endorsing reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can be unfair if studies are poor quality; risks rubber-stamping and reduced critical appraisal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer incentives — nonfinancial
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonfinancial incentives — frequent invitations, staying up-to-date, influence on science, improved reviewing acumen, free journal access, acknowledgement, certificates, editorial board appointment, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often feasible for journals; can increase engagement and recognition without monetary costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer incentives — crediting (DOI/ORCID)
rubrics_metrics.description: Crediting incentives — formal recognition of reviewing work, linking peer review activity to ORCID records using DOIs, publication of full reviews, awards and badges (e.g., Publons).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides career-relevant credit and visibility; may hasten review acceptance and improve transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer incentives — financial
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial incentives — payment for reviews, waivers of publication charges, or access to paid articles; some platforms (e.g., Rubriq) provide monetary compensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can hasten reviews but many journals cannot afford it; may affect review quality, transform review into a business, introduce fairness issues and moral concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer training via Publons / Publons Academy
rubrics_metrics.description: Publons/Publons Academy — platform for verifying and providing recognition of review activity and offering a free peer review training course on core competencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps train reviewers, increase review acceptance, hasten review time, improve review quality, and open access to reviewers' comments; awards and rankings may be included in CVs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core competency — written, unbiased, timely feedback to authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides written, unbiased feedback in timely manner on scholarly merits and scientific value of work (reviewer's responsibility to the authors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be constructive, focused on merits and scientific value, and delivered within agreed timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core competency — quality of review (constructive and fair)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides high-quality, constructive, and fair reviews (quality of review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate whether writing is clear, concise, and relevant; avoid ad hominem or nonconstructive criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core competency — evaluate clarity and relevance of writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicates whether writing is clear, concise, and relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment on presentation, clarity of argument, and whether the manuscript communicates findings appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core competency — maintain confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintains confidentiality of review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not disclose manuscript content or use unpublished results for personal advantage; respect embargoes and reviewer confidentiality policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core competency — impartiality and integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Makes comments and conclusions based on objective and impartial consideration of facts, exclusive of personal or professional bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid conflicts of interest, personal bias, and favoritism; base critique on evidence and methodologic grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core competency — timeliness and responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Timeliness and responsiveness (e.g., respond to invitations, meet deadlines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reveal any conflicts of interest promptly; accept review invitations only when able to complete them on time and with sufficient expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core competency — disclose conflicts of interest (to authors/editors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reveals/discloses any potential personal or financial conflicts of interest related to the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose to editors and where appropriate to authors; decline review if COI prevents objective evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core competency — comply with editor's instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Complies with editor's written instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow journal-specific guidance on scope, format, confidentiality, and timelines to ensure reviews meet editorial needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core competency — provide fair, constructive, and informative critique to editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides fair, constructive, and informative critique for editorial decision-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Help editors determine merit, originality, scope, and ethical concerns; be explicit about strengths, weaknesses, and suitability for journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core competency — determine merit, originality, and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Determines merit, originality, and scope of work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess novelty, contribution to field, and appropriate target audience or journal fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core competency — note ethical concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Notes any ethical concerns in the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag issues such as plagiarism, data fabrication, unethical human/animal research, authorship disputes, or undeclared conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core competency — accurate personal/professional information
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides personal and professional information that is accurate and fair representation of his/her expertise, including verifiable and accurate contact information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure editors can verify expertise and accountability; misrepresenting credentials undermines trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core competency — accountability to editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Accountability — responsible for making his/her competence clear to editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be transparent about areas of expertise and limits; decline if not qualified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core competency — methodology appraisal (to readers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensures that the study methods are adequately detailed (methodology appraisal for readers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for reproducibility, appropriate statistical methods, sample size justification, and clarity of experimental procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core competency — reference citation appraisal (to readers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensures that the article cites all relevant studies/reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify missing key literature, inappropriate citation practices, or over-reliance on low-quality sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess speed impact of innovations
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether peer review innovations reduce time to publication or shorten reviewing time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure time-to-decision, time-to-publication, incidence of redundant reviews; cascading and portable reviews aim to reduce delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess content and quality impact of innovations
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether innovations affect the content quality of published articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare methodological rigor, detection of errors/misconduct, and overall quality of accepted papers under new models versus traditional review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess bias reduction and accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether innovations and incentives have reduced bias against particular author groups and made publishing more accessible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine effects on gender/ethnicity/geography, on access for low-resource authors, and whether financial incentives create inequities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess effect on replication and negative results
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify whether innovations make it easier to publish replication studies, negative results, and contrarian hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track acceptance rates of replication/negative studies and whether models encourage impact-neutral review focusing on validity rather than novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess detection of scientific malpractice
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether innovations improve detection of scientific malpractice such as fabrication, plagiarism, or fake peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider use of independent validation services, scorecards, AI tools, and sharing of reviewer reports to enhance detection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess ability to keep readers abreast
rubrics_metrics.description: Judge whether innovations help readers stay informed of latest developments effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider discoverability, recommendation services, post-publication curation, and transparent review histories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer selection and guidance effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Guiding reviewers through the review process versus leaving them to decide affects ability to detect problematic publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full/good guidance is reported most effective in detecting problems; partial guidance appears least effective. Journal instructions and reviewer training should be scrutinized and improved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author-suggested reviewers (practice & effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Author-suggested reviewers — authors suggesting reviewers provide reports comparable in quality but more likely to recommend acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider making author-suggested reviewers optional or ceasing the practice to limit bias; monitor tendencies to recommend acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fake peer review and manipulation risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoidance/detection of fake peer review — manipulation by suggesting fake reviewers, peer circles, or paying agencies to fabricate reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize higher prevalence in some contexts (e.g., certain regions, low-impact journals); implement verification of reviewer identities, editorial vigilance, and integrity checks to prevent retractions and fabricated publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of social media for post-publication commentary
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of Twitter, blogs, and other social media to comment on published articles to increase transparency and wider involvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advantages: broader participation and openness. Risks: irrelevant comments from non-specialists; requires moderation and study to optimise usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprint repositories consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Role of biomedical preprint repositories as a publishing mechanism without traditional peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preprints speed communication and avoid reviewing delays but have not undergone formal peer review; implications for evidence-based medicine and public understanding must be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI-assisted peer review (future model)
rubrics_metrics.description: AI-assisted peer review — using AI for image recognition, recommending content, detecting fraud/plagiarism, or flagging issues; human final judgement required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can augment detection and efficiency but must be used with human oversight and validation of AI outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hybrid peer review platform (future model)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hybrid peer review — harmonisation, certification, and incentivisation combining elements of multiple models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims to blend strengths of models (e.g., openness and quality assurance) while offering incentives and certification for reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blockchain/tokenized peer review (future model)
rubrics_metrics.description: Blockchain model — technology for creating a tokenized peer review system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed for immutable records, crediting, and transparency; practical considerations and equity implications need evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portable/independent scorecards and validation services
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of scorecards and independent validation services to determine strengths and weaknesses and detect integrity issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercial platforms may provide structured evaluation checklists and validation separate from journals; can speed processes but raise commercialization concerns.
